Section 3 of title VI of article I of said Act is amended to read as follows:


“Sec. 3. 
Imposition and Rate of Tax.—

There is hereby annually levied and imposed for each taxable year upon the taxable income of every resident a tax at the following rates:
“One and one-half per centum on the first $5,000 of taxable income.
“Two per centum on the next $5,000 of taxable income.
“Two and one-half per centum on the next $5,000 of taxable income.
“Three per centum on the taxable income in excess of $15,000.”

fable.w: This section only amends a tax statute to set the rates of income tax levied on residents' taxable income. There is no tempting reading here: it contains no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a statutory tax rate schedule. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The text is purely prescriptive regarding financial obligations, not participatory mechanisms.
qwen_block.s: There is hereby annually levied and imposed for each taxable year upon the taxable income of every resident a tax at the following rates:

opus.w: The section amends a tax statute to set graduated income tax rates on residents' taxable income. It has no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. The fact that it imposes a government tax is not participation.
opus.b: The section only sets tax rates and creates no process involving outside parties. The likely trap is that "levied and imposed" sounds like a government decision. But nothing here calls for a comment period, rulemaking, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or a right to sue. The text is just a rate schedule.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes statutory tax rates for residents. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, public hearing, or advisory input from outside parties before the tax is imposed. The imposition of a tax is a unilateral legislative/executive action, not a participatory process involving outside entities in the decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: There is hereby annually levied and imposed for each taxable year upon the taxable income of every resident a tax at the following rates:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that taxing "residents" involves the public, and thus constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and more importantly, a tax levy is a unilateral imposition by the government, not a process of consultation, coordination, or advisory input from outside parties before a decision is made. The section merely sets statutory rates; it does not invite public comment, hearings, or advisory input.
